questions.q: Which test case specifically proves idempotency actually holds, not just in theory?
options: Successful sync
Expired OAuth token
Meridian HR unreachable
Duplicate employee ID — redelivering the same webhook twice
questions.explain: Redelivering the same webhook and confirming only one sys_user exists afterward is what actually proves the idempotency check works.

questions.q: In the background script, if `gs.info('Same record? ' + (firstSysId == secondSysId));` logs true, what does that confirm?
options: The REST Message failed on the second call
Both calls created separate sys_user records
Both calls returned the same sys_id, meaning the idempotency check correctly prevented a duplicate record
The OAuth token expired between the two calls
questions.explain: Matching sys_ids across both calls is the proof that creating the same employee twice doesn't produce two records.

questions.q: Why does testing "Meridian HR unreachable" need to confirm retries happen with increasing delay AND that the integration eventually gives up cleanly, rather than just confirming an error got logged somewhere?
options: Because logging alone doesn't prove the retry loop and its exponential backoff actually executed correctly before failing, with no partial record left behind
Because retries are not actually part of this integration
Because Meridian HR cannot return a 500 status code
Because a single failed attempt is always sufficient to prove resilience
questions.explain: A real test confirms the full retry behavior worked as designed, not just that some error eventually appeared in the log.

questions.q: What does testing an expired OAuth token confirm about RESTMessageV2 and the OAuth Entity Profile?
options: That the integration stops working entirely once a token expires
That a developer must manually request a new token in script
That RESTMessageV2 requests a fresh token automatically when the cached one expires, with no code change required
That OAuth tokens never actually expire in this integration
questions.explain: This test proves the token lifecycle the OAuth Entity Profile promised in Lesson 27 actually works under a real expiration.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does Course 8, ServiceNow ITSM Implementation, shift focus toward?
options: Building more REST integrations and webhook triggers
Implementing full incident, problem, and change management processes using the scripting and integration skills from this stage
Re-teaching JavaScript fundamentals from scratch
Replacing MID Servers with a newer integration pattern
questions.explain: The next course applies everything from this three-course Application Development stage to real ITSM process implementation.
